images.title: A high price isn't a high commission
images.alt: Comparison: a $2,000 laptop at a 2% rate earns $40, while a $300 software plan at 30% earns $90.

images.title: Which model fits your site right now
images.alt: Decision chart: broad traffic suits low ticket, a small specific audience you know well suits high ticket, and neither means start low ticket in one category.
images.caption: Match the model to how your readers already buy, not to the size of the commission.

data.question: What does your site have today?

branches.result: Low ticket. Roundups and quick comparisons for readers who buy fast.
High ticket, if you can answer the hard questions before a big purchase.
Start low ticket in one narrow category and add higher offers later.

images.after: Refunds and held commissions hurt more at high ticket
images.title: Compare high-ticket programs past the rate
images.alt: Checklist for comparing high-ticket affiliate programs: refund window, hold period, one-time or recurring payout, and trial cancellations.
images.caption: A lower rate that's paid reliably can be worth more than a higher one that keeps getting reversed.

items: How long is the refund window?
How long are commissions held before they're payable?
Is the payout one-time or recurring?
Do trial cancellations or early refunds earn you nothing?
Read the program's own rules, since every program sets its own
